# AAL test 2 protocol (pre-registered)

**Registered:** 2026-11-11, after test 1 and the declaration of R-W3, before the test 2 data exist and before R-W3 ran on any real run. **Author:** Claude (PM). **Owner mandate:** "the correct result, not the one we want" (2026-11-11).

## Part S2: harder synthetic cases, honesty of intervals

**Data.** Four cases generated by `tools/synth_flame_profiles.py` (v2, which reproduces the test 1 data byte for byte) after this protocol is sealed. Parameters are drawn at random within the ranges below by `tools/make_test2_truth.py`; the truth file is withheld and its SHA-256 sealed.

| Case | Stress | Estimand interval |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | asymmetric leading edge (Richards curve) that sharpens | air display 3 |
| T2 | edge that broadens, with frame-to-frame brightness flicker | air display 3 |
| T3 | pre-burn reference frame followed by a long gap (as in B11); short flow segments | air display 2 |
| T4 | luminous edge that drifts relative to the true front | air display 3 |

**Truth.** The speed of the generator's true front during the estimand interval. In T4 the luminous edge is offset from the true front by an amount that changes during the interval, so no definition based on luminosity alone tracks the truth exactly; an analyst who states that this offset is unknown, or widens the interval for it, is behaving correctly.

**Analysts.** GFL R-W3 (frozen before the data exist); gpt-5.5, gpt-6-astra, grok-4.7, Kimi-K2.6 (same prompt, direct to Foundry); Manus (temporary cloud computer, full package). Wording fixed after ISS-046: the Python standard library is allowed; no third-party package other than numpy and pandas.

**Metrics.** Primary: **coverage**, the share of the eight case results whose reported 95 % interval contains the truth (nominal 95 %; below 75 % means the intervals are overconfident). Secondary: relative error, re-execution (the script reproduces its printed values), labelling, direction, and whether the T4 offset problem and the T3 pre-burn gap are named. Re-execution by GFL with `python -I` in an empty environment.

## Part R: predictions on real runs under R-W3 (sealed before any R-W3 run on real data)

Basis: thin-fuel thermal regime (de Ris; Bhattacharjee et al. 2016), where the spread rate does not depend on the opposing-flow speed and scales inversely with fuel thickness. All predictions are ratios to B6's R-W3 reference rate at air display 3, so they do not depend on the B6 value itself, which R-W3 has not yet produced.

| ID | Run | Prediction | Band |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-B9 | B9: 100 µm, 20 mm, 21 % O₂, air display 2 | same rate as B6 (flow independence) | ratio 0.85–1.15 |
| P-B11a | B11: 200 µm, air display 2 | half of B6 (inverse thickness) | ratio 0.425–0.575 |
| P-B11b | B11: air display 0 vs display 2 | slower at display 0 (towards the radiative and transport-limited regime) | rate(0) < rate(2), intervals not overlapping |
| P-B13 | B13: 400 µm, air display 3 | a quarter of B6 (inverse thickness, if still thermally thin) | ratio 0.2125–0.2875 |

Each prediction is reported as supported, not supported, or not testable (no segment passing the gates, or a run identity not confirmed: B9's NEF archive was assigned by time order, ISS-032, and must be confirmed from EXIF and the proof sheet before use). Not testable is never counted as supported. B9, B13 and the B9 and B13 videos and proof sheets are acquired after this protocol is anchored.

## What does not change during the test

R-W3, the metrics, the bands and the task text. Deviations are recorded as deviations.
